See also: Laine, làine, and láine

English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

laine (plural laines)

  1. (Sussex) an area of arable land at the foot of a hill

See also

[edit]
  • mousseline de laine
  • satin de laine

Anagrams

[edit]
  • linea, Alien, elain, anile, Aline, alien, liane, Eilan, Elian, Elina, aline, A-line, Elain, Nelia

laine (genitive laine, partitive lainet)

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *lainëh, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlainiz (“leaning”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlɑi̯neˣ/, [ˈlɑ̝i̯ne̞(ʔ)]
  • Rhymes: -ɑine
  • Syllabification(key): lai‧ne
  • Hyphenation(key): lai‧ne

Noun

[edit]

laine

  1. wave
    Synonym: aalto

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French laine, from Old French lainne, lein, from Latin lāna.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /lɛn/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛn

Noun

[edit]

laine f (plural laines)

  1. wool

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bas de laine
  • laine de fer
  • laine de verre
  • pure laine

Related terms

[edit]
  • laineux
  • lainier

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Cantonese: 冷 (laang5-1)
  • → Vietnamese: len

Further reading

[edit]
  • “laine”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Aline, enlia

Ingrian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *lainëh. Cognates include Finnish laine and Estonian laine.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Ala-Laukaa) IPA(key): /ˈlɑi̯ne/, [ˈɫɑi̯n]
  • (Soikkola) IPA(key): /ˈlɑi̯ne/, [ˈɫɑi̯ne̞]
  • Rhymes: -ɑi̯n, -ɑi̯ne
  • Hyphenation: lai‧ne
  • Homophone: laina

Noun

[edit]

laine

  1. wave

Declension

[edit]
Declension of laine (type 6/lähe, no gradation)
singular plural
nominative laine laineet
genitive laineen lainein

illative laineesse laineisse

ablative laineelt laineilt
translative laineeks laineiks
essive laineenna, laineen laineinna, lainein
exessive1) laineent laineint

*) the accusative corresponds with either the genitive (sg) or nominative (pl)
**) the comitative is formed by adding the suffix -ka? or -kä? to the genitive.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • alto

Derived terms

[edit]
  • emälaine
  • heinälaine

References

[edit]
  • V. I. Junus (1936), Iƶoran Keelen Grammatikka‎[2], Leningrad: Riikin Ucebno-pedagogiceskoi Izdateljstva, page 7
  • Ruben E. Nirvi (1971), Inkeroismurteiden Sanakirja, Helsinki: Suomalais-Ugrilainen Seura, page 244

Norman

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French lainne, leine, from Latin lāna.

Noun

[edit]

laine f (plural laines)

  1. (Jersey) wool
